newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha firmer, inter-month spreads stable.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha firmer, inter-month spreads stable.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices climbed for the second consecutive day on Tuesday because of tight supplies combined with firm crude oil prices, traders said.

Although most market participants are expected to square their positions ahead of Christmas and year-end holidays, activity remained largely quiet in afternoon trading due to overnight crude surges, they said.
"People were made nervous by the crude movement," one trader said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half February was assessed at $238.00/240.00. It was traded at $234.00 on Monday.
First-half March was notionally quoted at $234.00/237.00, compared with $230.00/232.00 in late Monday trading.
The one-month spread from first-half February was virtually unchanged from Monday levels at plus $6.00/8.00.
In the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, spot cargoes were quoted over $27.00 per barrel on a cost and freight (C and F) basis, traders said.
The current levels, which are about $3.00 a barrel higher than a week ago, kept regional LSWR buyers on the sidelines, they said.
